original: We propose an imperceptible multi-bit text watermark embedded by paraphrasing with LLMs. We fine-tune a pair of LLM paraphrasers that are designed to behave differently so that their paraphrasing difference reflected in the text semantics can be identified by a trained decoder. To embed our multi-bit watermark, we use two paraphrasers alternatively to encode the pre-defined binary code at the sentence level. Then we use a text classifier as the decoder to decode each bit of the watermark. Through extensive experiments, we show that our watermarks can achieve over 99.99\% detection AUC with small (1.1B) text paraphrasers while keeping the semantic information of the original sentence. More importantly, our pipeline is robust under word substitution and sentence paraphrasing perturbations and generalizes well to out-of-distributional data. We also show the stealthiness of our watermark with LLM-based evaluation. We open-source the code: this https URL.
text: We introduce an imperceptible multi-bit text watermark through paraphrasing with LLMs. To achieve this, we fine-tune a pair of LLM paraphrasers that are designed to have differences in behavior in order to reflect their semantic differences in the text. To embed our multi-bit watermark, we alternate two paraphrasers to encode a predetermined binary code at the sentence level. Then, we use a text classifier as the decoder to decode each bit of the watermark. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that our watermarks can achieve over 99.99% detection AUC with small (1.1B) text paraphrasers, while maintaining the original sentence's semantic information. Significantly, our pipeline is robust under word substitutions and sentence paraphrasing perturbations, exhibiting strong generalization capabilities for out-of-distributional data. We also demonstrate the stealthiness of our watermark with LLM-based evaluation. Our code is now available to the public: this https URL

text: We propose a technique for embedding imperceptible multi-bit text watermarks using paraphrasing with Language Models (LLMs). A pair of paraphrasers is fine-tuned which behave differently from each other. Their paraphrasing differences, which are subtle, can be detected by a trained decoder due to variations in text semantics. We use a text classifier as our decoder system to decode the multi-bit watermark after applying alternative paraphrasers on predefined sentence level data. Experimental results demonstrate that our watermarks can achieve a detection AUC of over 99.99% even with small (1.1B) paraphrasing models, while the original sentence's semantic content remains intact. An additional benefit is the robustness of our method in resisting word substitutions, sentence-level paraphrases etc. , as well as generalizing effectively to new data. The stealthiness of the watermark is also confirmed by LLM-based evaluations. We released the code online for further research here: this https URL

text: We present a stealthy multi-bit text watermarking method that leverages paraphrasing with LLMs. To do this, we fine-tune a pair of LLM paraphrasing models designed to behave differently, whose paraphrasing divergence in the text can be detected through a skilled decoder. For the watermark embedding, we alternate the use of the two paraphrasers to encode a pre-defined binary code at the sentence level. We use a text classifier as the decoder to demarcate each bit of the watermark. Through extensive testing, we demonstrate that our watermarks can achieve over 99.99% detection AUC with small (1.1B) text paraphrasing models, while preserving the original semantic content. Our pipeline also exhibits resilience against word substitution and sentence rephrasing perturbations, providing good generalization across out-of-distributional data. Additionally, we validate the stealth of our watermark with an LLM-based assessment. The source code for this is publicly available: [this link provided].

text: We introduce an imperceptible multi-bit text watermarking method using paraphrasing with LLMs. We train a pair of LLM paraphrasers in such a way that they differ in their behavior and their paraphrasing differences can be detected by a trained decoder because of the difference shown in the text semantics. For embedding the multi-bit watermark, we alternate using these two paraphrasers to encode pre-defined binary codes at the sentence level. To decode each bit of the watermark, we use a text classifier as a decoder to detect them. Through thorough experiments, we demonstrate that our watermarks can achieve over 99.99% detection AUC using relatively small (1.1B) text paraphrasers while preserving the semantic content of the original sentences. More importantly, our pipeline is robust under changes caused by words being substituted and sentences being rephrased, as well as easily handling data from outside the training environment. We also show the subtle nature of our watermark with evaluations based on LLMs. The code source is available: this https URL.

original: 我们提出了一种通过大语言模型（LLMs）改写嵌入的多比特文本水印方法。我们微调了两个基于LLM的文本改写器，使其改写后文本语义上的差异能够被训练好的解码器识别。为了嵌入多比特水印，我们在句子层面交替使用两个改写器来编码预定义的二进制码。随后，我们使用文本分类器作为解码器来解码水印的每一比特。通过大量实验，我们展示了使用规模较小（1.1B参数）改写器时，水印检测的AUC可达99.99%以上，同时保持了原句的语义信息。更重要的是，我们的方法在词语替换和句子改写扰动下具有鲁棒性，并且能良好泛化到分布外数据。我们还通过基于LLM的评估展示了水印的隐蔽性。代码已开源，链接为：https URL。
